name: Faye Wong
who_line: Hong Kong had turned her into a dress hanger. New York showed her people who did not care.
who: Faye Wong is the Cantopop singer who treated the stage like an avant-garde closet before that was a sport. Stylists Thomas Chan and Titi Kwan chose the houses. She almost never explains the clothes.

The usable English line is about New York, 1996. She told Time Asia she sat in cafes and watched strange, confident-looking people who did not care what others thought. In Hong Kong she had been shaped into a machine, a dress hanger. The archival avant-garde — Westwood, Yohji, Margiela, Helmut Lang, later Philo Céline — is what that refusal looked like on a Cantopop stage.
work: She covered Teresa Teng; Cocteau Twins wrote for Fuzao; she has named them among her favourite bands. Cranberries and Tori Amos covers sit next to Buddhist songs and a 2001 charity album. The record, not the fashion interview, is where the influences are named.
English first-person fashion quotes are scarce. Do not invent a manifesto. Do not put the stylists’ house names in her mouth.

quotes.text: I wandered around, visited museums and sat at cafes. There were so many strange, confident-looking people. They didn’t care what other people thought of them. I felt I was originally like that too, independent and a little rebellious. But in Hong Kong I lost myself. I was shaped by others and became like a machine, a dress hanger. I had no personality and no sense of direction.
quotes.said_to: Anthony Spaeth, Time Asia, “She Did It Her Way” (print; circulating via Wikipedia and SCMP)

why_the_look: Hong Kong had turned her into a dress hanger. New York showed her people who did not care. The archival avant-garde is what that refusal looked like on a Cantopop stage.
beliefs: Named influences in the record: Teresa Teng; Cocteau Twins; The Cranberries / Tori Amos covers. Buddhist since the early 1990s. Stylists Thomas Chan and Titi Kwan chose the houses.
